title: Registering step by step and setting up properly

say: Registering step by step, and setting up properly.
This is the video for module two of Business Registration and Compliance in Nigeria.
You can register a business name yourself on the CAC portal, from cac.gov.ng. Screens change, so follow the labels you see on the day.
Step one. Create your account with your own email and phone, never an agent's.

She re-signed in black pen on white paper, corrected her surname letter for letter, resubmitted, and was approved two days later without paying again.

say: A company needs more decisions: name ending in Limited, address, share capital, shareholders, directors, and people with significant control.
For example, Chioma and her sister Adaeze in Enugu are registering a catering company.

say: Chioma runs it full time and puts in 700,000 naira, so she takes 700,000 shares of 1 naira each. That is 70 percent.

card.title: Splitting shares in a company
card.note: Issued share capital: shares of 1 naira each.

say: Adaeze puts in 300,000 naira and takes 300,000 shares, 30 percent.

card.title: Splitting shares in a company

say: Their issued share capital is 1,000,000 naira, matching what they put in. Stamp duty is charged on share capital, so choose a figure you can justify.
Both are directors, and they sign a short private agreement on what happens if one sister leaves.

say: Many owners use an accredited agent for a company. Ask for their accreditation number and check it on the CAC website. Insist the portal account and email are yours.

panel.heading: Ask before you pay
items: Are you accredited by the CAC?
Will the account and email be mine?
CAC fee and your fee, in writing?
Will I get every document after approval?
Who files my annual returns, and when?

say: Ask for the CAC fee and their fee separately, in writing, and for every document after approval.
And never let someone register the company in their name on your behalf. The person on the register is the legal owner. Your name, your NIN, your shares.

panel.rule: Business money goes in and out of the business account only.

say: Here is a worked example. Rukayat in Ilorin gives customers only her business account number.
In her first month, customers pay 185,000 naira.
She pays 112,000 for flour, sugar, gas and packaging from the business account, and keeps every receipt.
At month end she pays herself a fixed 40,000 naira, recorded as owner's drawings.
That leaves 33,000 naira in the business. Her real profit is 185,000 minus 112,000, which is 73,000 naira, and her bank statement now supports any loan or tax filing.
To remember. Match your NIN exactly. Fix only what a query asks. Shares divide ownership. Keep the account, email and shares in your own name. And separate business money from day one.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Your details must match your NIN exactly
Answer queries by fixing only what is asked
Shares divide ownership: 700,000 of 1,000,000 is 70%
The account, email and shares stay in your name
Separate business and personal money from day one
